2616-memoirs-of-general-william-t-sherma.title: Memoirs Of General William T Sherman Volume 1
2616-memoirs-of-general-william-t-sherma.creator: William T. Sherman
2616-memoirs-of-general-william-t-sherma.description: A book by William T. Sherman. In this free country every man is at perfect liberty to publish his own thoughts and impressions, and any witness who may differ from me should publish his own version of facts in the truthful narration of which he is interested. I am publishing my own memoirs, not theirs, and we all know that no three honest witnesses of a simple brawl can agree on all the details.

arxiv-2103-06325.title: Charge density waves and electronic properties of superconducting kagome metals
arxiv-2103-06325.creator: Hengxin Tan, Yizhou Liu, Ziqiang Wang, Binghai Yan
arxiv-2103-06325.description: Abstract Kagome metals A A V 3 Sb 5 ( A = A= K, Rb, and Cs) exhibit intriguing superconductivity below 0.9 ∼ 2.5 0.9\sim 2.5 K, a charge density wave (CDW) transition around 80 ∼ 100 80\sim 100 K, and ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} topological surface states. The nature of the CDW phase and its relation to superconductivity remains elusive.

arxiv-2105-10940.title: Perspective: Nonlinear Hall Effects
arxiv-2105-10940.creator: Z. Z. Du, Hai-Zhou Lu, X. C. Xie
arxiv-2105-10940.description: Abstract The Hall effects comprise one of the oldest but most vital fields in condensed matter physics, and they persistently inspire new findings such as quantum Hall effects and topological phases of matter. The recently discovered nonlinear Hall effect is a new member of the family of Hall effects.

arxiv-2111-09035.title: Multi-Attribute Relation Extraction (MARE) - Simplifying the Application of Relation Extraction
arxiv-2111-09035.creator: Lars Klöser 1 , Philipp Kohl 1 , Bodo Kraft 1 and Albert Zündorf 2 1 FH Aachen, University of Applied Sciences, Germany 2 University of Kassel, Germany { kloeser, p.kohl, kraft } @fh-aachen.de, zuendorf@uni-kassel.de
arxiv-2111-09035.description: Abstract Natural language understanding’s relation extraction makes innovative and encouraging novel business concepts possible and facilitates new digitilized decision-making processes. Current approaches allow the extraction of relations with a fixed number of entities as attributes. Extracting relations with an arbitrary amount of attributes requires complex systems and costly relation-trigger annotations to assist these systems.

arxiv-2201-12677.title: AIM : An Adaptive and Iterative Mechanism for Differentially Private Synthetic Data
arxiv-2201-12677.creator: Ryan McKenna, Brett Mullins, Daniel Sheldon, Gerome Miklau
arxiv-2201-12677.description: Abstract . We propose AIM , a new algorithm for differentially private synthetic data generation. AIM is a workload-adaptive algorithm within the paradigm of algorithms that first selects a set of queries, then privately measures those queries, and finally generates synthetic data from the noisy measurements.

arxiv-2210-05309.title: Optimization of laser stabilization via self-injection locking to a whispering-gallery-mode microresonator: experimental study Journal: oe
arxiv-2210-05309.creator: Artem E. Shitikov, 1,* Ilya I. Lykov, 1 Oleg V. Benderov, 2 Dmitry A. Chermoshentsev, 1,2,3 Ilya K. Gorelov, 1,4 Andrey N. Danilin, 1,4 Ramzil R. Galiev, 5 Nikita M. Kondratiev, 5 Steevy J. Cordette, 5 Alexander V. Rodin, 2 Anatoly V. Masalov, 1,6 Valery E. Lobanov, 1 Igor A. Bilenko, 1,4
arxiv-2210-05309.description: Abstract Self-injection locking of a diode laser to a high-quality-factor microresonator is widely used for frequency stabilization and linewidth narrowing. We constructed several microresonator-based laser sources with measured instantaneous linewidths of 1 Hz and used them for investigation and implementation of the self-injection locking effect.

arxiv-2210-14981.title: Fast and Efficient Scene Categorization for Autonomous Driving using VAEs
arxiv-2210-14981.creator: Saravanabalagi Ramachandran, Jonathan Horgan, Ganesh Sistu, John McDonald
arxiv-2210-14981.description: Abstract Scene categorization is a useful precursor task that provides prior knowledge for many advanced computer vision tasks with a broad range of applications in content-based image indexing and retrieval systems. Despite the success of data driven approaches in the field of computer vision such as object detection, semantic segmentation, etc.

arxiv-2308-15603.title: k k -tuple domination on Kneser graphs Partially supported by PIP CONICET 1900, PICT-2020-03032 and PID 80020210300068UR.
arxiv-2308-15603.creator: Maria Gracia Cornet, Pablo Torres
arxiv-2308-15603.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Maria Gracia Cornet, Pablo Torres. This paper considers multiple domination on Kneser graphs. We focus on k k -tuple dominating sets, 2 2 -packings and the associated graph parameters k k -tuple domination number and 2 2 -packing number.

arxiv-2412-12877.title: PRIMEdit: Probability Redistribution for Instance-aware Multi-object Video Editing with a New Benchmark Dataset
arxiv-2412-12877.creator: Samuel Teodoro, Agus Gunawan, Soo Ye Kim, Jihyong Oh, Munchurl Kim, School of Electrical Engineering, Korea Advanced Institute of Science, Technology
arxiv-2412-12877.description: Abstract Recent Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based video editing has enabled users to edit videos through simple text prompts, significantly simplifying the editing process. However, recent zero-shot video editing techniques focus on global or single-object edits, which can lead to unintended changes in other parts of the video.

arxiv-2504-19560.title: Strongly regular graphs from hyperbolic quadrics and their maximal cliques
arxiv-2504-19560.creator: Antonio Cossidente, Jan De Beule, Giuseppe Marino, Francesco Pavese, Valentino Smaldore
arxiv-2504-19560.description: Abstract Let Q + ​ ( 2 ​ n + 1 , q ) Q^{+}(2n+1,q) be a hyperbolic quadric of PG ⁡ ( 2 ​ n + 1 , q ) {\rm PG}(2n+1,q) . Fix a generator Π \Pi of the quadric.

arxiv-2509-22277.title: Online Firefighting on Cactus Graphs
arxiv-2509-22277.creator: Max Hugen, Bob Krekelberg, Alison Hsiang-Hsuan Liu
arxiv-2509-22277.description: Abstract The firefighting game is an important problem in theoretical computer science. It has been broadly studied in the offline model, including results on computational complexity for various graph classes. In this work, we investigate the online setting and the competitive complexity , which has been relatively less explored.

arxiv-2601-04025.title: Simulated Students in Tutoring Dialogues: Substance or Illusion?
arxiv-2601-04025.creator: Alexander Scarlatos, Jaewook Lee, Simon Woodhead, Andrew Lan
arxiv-2601-04025.description: Abstract Advances in large language models (LLMs) enable many new innovations in education. However, evaluating the effectiveness of new technology requires real students, which is time-consuming and hard to scale up. Therefore, many recent works on LLM-powered tutoring solutions have used simulated students for both training and evaluation, often via simple prompting.

pmc-10552930.title: Radiotherapy Versus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer
pmc-10552930.creator: Drashti Patel, Surekha Tayade, Vaishali P Tidke, Shikha Toshniwal, Hard Tilva
pmc-10552930.description: Eighty percent of women who have cervical cancer present at such an alarmingly advanced stage leading to high morbidity and mortality. Due to a lack of public awareness and inadequate infrastructure for screening and early identification in resource-poor countries like India, this tardy presentation is anticipated to continue in the future.

pmc-10680994.title: Association between Average Vitamin D Levels and COVID-19 Mortality in 19 European Countries—A Population-Based Study
pmc-10680994.creator: Amar S. Ahmad, Nirmin F. Juber, Heba Al-Naseri, Christian Heumann, Raghib Ali, Tim Oliver
pmc-10680994.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Early epidemic reports have linked low average 25(OH) vitamin D levels with increased COVID-19 mortality. However, there has been limited updated research on 25(OH) vitamin D and its impact on COVID-19 mortality. This study aimed to update the initial report studying the link between vitamin D deficiency and COVID-19 mortality by using multi-country data in 19 European countries up to the middle of June 2023.

pmc-11627008.title: Mood regulation in euthymic patients with a history of antidepressant‐induced mania
pmc-11627008.creator: Ramzi Halabi, Khairatun Yusuff, Clara Park, Alexandra DeShaw, Christina Gonzalez‐Torres, Muhammad I Husain, Claire O'Donovan, Martin Alda, Benoit H Mulsant, Abigail Ortiz
pmc-11627008.description: IntroductionThe use of antidepressants in bipolar disorder (BD) remains contentious, in part due to the risk of antidepressant‐induced mania (AIM). However, there is no information on the architecture of mood regulation in patients who have experienced AIM. We compared the architecture of mood regulation in euthymic patients with and without a history of AIM.MethodsEighty‐four euthymic participants were included.

pmc-11675047.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Combining with Imaging Analysis for Lesion Detection of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis in Children
pmc-11675047.creator: Siying Liu, Yongbing Zhu, Yu Chen, Yaqin Wang, Dedong Zhang, Jiasi Zhang, Yao Wang, Ai Zhang, Qun Hu, Aiguo Liu, Maura Massimino, Anna Lewandowska
pmc-11675047.description: Background: The detection of mutations from circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) represents a promising enrichment technique. In this retrospective study, the significance of ctDNA and imaging in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) monitoring was first examined, and the broader role of ctDNA in monitoring LCH was additionally explored.

pmc-12692304.title: Satellite DNA Genomics: The Ongoing Story
pmc-12692304.creator: Manuel A Garrido-Ramos, Miroslav Plohl, Eva Šatović-Vukšić, Salvatore Saccone
pmc-12692304.description: Tandemly repeated non-coding sequences, widely known as satellite DNAs (satDNAs), are extremely diverse and highly variable components of eukaryotic genomes. In recent years, advances in high-throughput sequencing and new bioinformatics platforms have enabled in-depth studies of all (or nearly all) tandem repeats in any genome (the satellitome), while a growing number of telomere-to-telomere assemblies facilitates their detailed mapping.

pmc-12972541.title: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on end-of-life care in LTCFs in England: A qualitative study of LTCF staff experiences
pmc-12972541.creator: Natalie Cotterell, Danni Collingridge Moore
pmc-12972541.description: Background:The COVID-19 pandemic significantly increased the number of deaths within long-term care facilities (LTCFs) globally. Restrictions around visitation and social distancing were common; however, research conducted during the pandemic demonstrates that these policies impacted the ways in which end-of-life care was delivered in LTCFs.

pmc-13074556.title: Genomic Footprints of Multiple Host Lineages in the Mitochondrial and Nuclear Genomes of the Holoparasite Prosopanche americana
pmc-13074556.creator: Laura E. Garcia, Maria Emilia Roulet, Lucía A. Garay, M. Virginia Sanchez-Puerta
pmc-13074556.description: Horizontal Gene Transfer (HGT) is a hallmark of the evolution of parasitic plants, facilitated by the haustorial connection. While mitochondrial HGT is widespread, the extent of nuclear HGT and the long-term retention of foreign genetic material in holoparasitic lineages remain poorly understood. This study explores the genomic architecture of Prosopanche americana (Hydnoraceae), a non-photosynthetic holoparasite currently specialized on Fabaceae.

pmc-13193866.title: Ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis in melanoma: regulatory cell death pathways and their implications for immunotherapy
pmc-13193866.creator: Qingyi Wang, Jian Zhu
pmc-13193866.description: Melanoma is a highly aggressive skin malignancy with poor prognosis in advanced stages. Despite significant breakthroughs achieved by immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) such as PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockers, challenges including heterogeneous treatment responses, acquired resistance, and immune-related toxicities remain prominent.

pmc-13238576.title: Emergency Department Presentations During Dry and Humid Heatwaves: A Case‐Crossover Study in the Northern Territory, Australia
pmc-13238576.creator: Rowena Boyd, Alyson Wright, Nicolas Borchers‐Arriagada, Paul Fox‐Hughes, Fay H Johnston, Paul Burgess, Tracy Ward, Sharon L Campbell
pmc-13238576.description: In a rapidly warming climate, heatwaves pose an increasing threat to human health. However, there is limited knowledge of heatwave impacts on health outcomes, or the role of humidity in the tropical and arid climates of Australia's Northern Territory (NT).

pmc-13330467.title: Analysis and interpretation of the heterogeneity of community-based health insurance attributes and preferences in Senegal: evidence from a discrete choice experiment
pmc-13330467.creator: Oumar Sagna
pmc-13330467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionCommunity-based health insurance (CBHI) schemes have been widely promoted to improve financial protection and expand access to healthcare in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly among populations working in the informal sector who lack access to formal health insurance. In Sub-Saharan Africa, CBHI has been implemented as part of broader efforts to advance universal health coverage (UHC), yet enrolment often remains low.

pmc-13424489.title: Validation of self-reported family history of myocardial infarction using nationwide health care data
pmc-13424489.creator: Agnes Wahrenberg, Karin Leander, Henrike Häbel, Patrik K. E. Magnusson, Ralf Kuja-Halkola, Göran Bergström, Lars Lind, Emil Hagström, Gunnar Engström, Tomas Jernberg, Stefan Söderberg, Carl Johan Östgren, Per Svensson
pmc-13424489.description: Self-reported family history of myocardial infarction (MI) is frequently used to assess cardiovascular risk. However, validation of self-reported family history has often been limited to small samples, and to death-certificates or self-reported medical history as reference. This study investigated the accuracy of self-reported family history of MI in a population-based cohort, using register data as reference.
